subject: FinTechCo — Post-demo: API auth & key management next steps

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>

Subject: FinTechCo — Post-demo: API auth & key management next steps

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — appreciate the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on the API authentication and key management items we discussed:

Recap:
- You want a short-term path to integrate quickly (API keys) and a longer-term, more secure approach (service accounts + JWT/OAuth) for internal microservices.
- Key rotation and auditing (rotation cadence, vault/KMS integration, and audit logs) are gating requirements for your security team.
- You asked about scoped keys for embeddings/rerank endpoints and per-route routing to lower-cost model variants.

Proposed next steps:
1) I shared a short playbook (attached) with our recommended auth patterns — can you confirm which of these you'd like to trial?
2) We propose a 2-week POC scope: SDK integration on a sandbox project (API key auth), and a parallel design review for service-account + JWT flow for production. I'll attach a draft mutual action plan for dates and owners.
3) Security questionnaire: Priya, if you can share your SOC/Security checklist items we should prioritize, Rishi will pair with your team next week.

Questions for you:
- Do you have a preferred KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HashiVault) for key storage?
- For embeddings/reranking, would you prefer per-tenant keys or a single service account with scoped tokens?

I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up next week — propose Tuesday 11am PT unless that conflicts.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0187

Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinTechCo — Post-demo: API auth & key management next steps

Thanks Marissa — solid recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- We use AWS KMS today, so that would be the preferred KMS for production.
- For the POC, per-tenant keys may be heavy; we were thinking a service account + scoped JWT for the middle-tier (our API) and short-lived API keys for internal dev sandbox access.
- Security wants rotation cadence guidance (30/90/180 days). Could you include recommended rotation intervals for API keys vs service account credentials in the playbook?

Tuesday 11am PT works for Alex + Priya. Can you send a calendar invite?

Appreciate it — Alex

--
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering
FinTechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com

Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinTechCo — Post-demo: API auth & key management next steps

Great, thanks for the details Alex. Short update & what I'll bring to Tuesday's call: 

What I'll bring:
- Updated playbook (attached) with explicit rotation recommendations: short-lived API keys (30 days rotation cadence recommended for dev/sandbox), service-account JWTs with 90-day rotation for key material and encourage short-lived signed tokens (<= 1 hour) issued by your token service.
- Sample SDK snippets showing:
  * SDK client initialization with API key 
  * JWT bearer flow for server-to-server calls
  * Example of per-request model routing header for embeddings vs generation endpoints
  * Structured output examples showing tool-calling placeholder for downstream callouts (simple JSON schema + content-type enforcement)
- Draft mutual action plan with milestones: POC start, sandbox SDK integration, security review, and production design review.

Notes on architecture choices:
- For embeddings/rerank: recommend service-account issued short-lived tokens that are scoped to the embeddings role; generates easier auditing and avoids proliferating static keys per tenant. If you need strict tenant isolation during POC, we can support per-tenant API keys in the sandbox.
- For key storage: our integrations are tested with AWS KMS and HashiCorp Vault; we'll provide examples for both.
- For rotation automation: we recommend using your KMS to store key material and our SDK's key-hook to fetch rotated keys; we can share a small script that rotates a key and updates the sandbox creds.

Action items (owners):
- Marissa: Update playbook & send calendar invite (today) — DONE (invite sent). Attached updated docs.
- Alex/Priya: Confirm POC sandbox owner + provide access to AWS KMS test key/ARN by EOD Monday.
- Rishi: Join Tuesday call for architecture deep-dive and audit-log questions.

If that looks good, we'll kick off the POC Tuesday.

Best,

Marissa

Quick ask for Alex/Priya: please share the AWS account ID and a test KMS ARN that we can use in the sandbox (we'll only use a test key and will not touch prod keys). Also, any existing SAML/OAuth issuer metadata if you plan to use your identity provider for issuing service account tokens.

See you Tuesday.
